cross_file_coordination.justification: While the diff correctly coordinates changes between core.py and formatting.py for its own purpose, it has zero coordination with the actual smell location. The feature envy code in Command's parameter resolution logic is untouched, as is the _last_state storage in parser.py.

structural_soundness.justification: The refactoring shown (extracting help text limit calculation to HelpFormatter) is structurally sound for what it does - it properly encapsulates formatting logic in the formatter class. However, this is irrelevant to the feature envy smell being evaluated.

code_quality.justification: The code quality of the changes shown is good - clear method name, proper documentation, reasonable abstraction. However, this quality assessment is meaningless since the changes don't address the smell at all.

data_locality_and_delegation.justification: No improvement to data locality. The Command class still accesses parser._short_opt, parser._long_opt, parser._args, and parser._last_state.opts. No delegation pattern is introduced to address the feature envy.

responsibility_allocation_and_cohesion.justification: No responsibility reallocation occurs. The logic for building _parser_known_dests and accessing parser internals remains in the Command class. The parser doesn't gain any new methods to encapsulate this responsibility.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring is completely unrelated to the feature envy smell. It improves help text formatting logic but leaves all the problematic parser internal accesses in the Command class untouched. The smell remains at 100% severity.
